A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2D work and include the main text and Appendices A–E. The scientific material supports reliable comparison, including text recoverable from v4's overlapping algorithm layout. Added experiments, relocated material, and the removed checklist are identifiable.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original eICU and Lacuna-100 experiments, including classification AUC, membership inference attacks, and computation times.

after.justification: v6 retains those empirical results and adds checkpoint-reconstruction experiments, an Alpaca LLM unlearning experiment, and t-SNE visualizations.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same learning, checkpoint rewinding, retained-data gradient descent, Gaussian perturbation, and proximal reconstruction procedures. Algorithm 3's variable renaming and the additional LoRA-based evaluation do not introduce a new R2D update or component.

E1.justification: v6 retains eICU patient and Lacuna-100 celebrity unlearning and adds Alpaca math-task removal during LLM instruction tuning (Appendix B.4). This introduces language generation and task-category forgetting beyond the original binary classification settings.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing comparisons retain HF, CNS, Finetune, Fisher Forgetting, SCRUB, and retraining. The new LLM experiment uses finetuning and retraining baselines already represented in v4; it introduces no additional comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 introduces Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 with LoRA, three training epochs, one- or two-epoch rewind continuations, and forget-set BLEU evaluation. Appendix B.3 adds Euclidean reconstruction-error measurement and reconstruction-inclusive timing. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the existing classifier settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v6 adds a substantive evaluation of the previously untested proximal reconstruction option, measuring checkpoint error and computational overhead across rewind depths (B.3, Tables 8–10). Figure 5 adds before/after t-SNE analysis. The existing noise, privacy, and rewind-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-fold cross-validation repeated ten times, 100 undersampling repetitions for classic MIA, the same noise-seed practice, and one-sigma MIA deviations. The new reconstruction and LLM tables provide point estimates without introducing additional uncertainty reporting or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: v6 adds reconstruction errors and timings, storage figures, and LLM outcomes. Table 11 reports forget-set BLEU of 0.1009 for R2D 33% versus 0.1035 for finetuning, each using one unlearning epoch. Existing benchmark scores are unchanged, including v4 Tables 8–11 matched to v6 Tables 12–15.

T1.justification: The main theorems and guarantees remain unchanged. v6 corrects a gradient's iterate argument in the proof of Lemma A.3 and removes Appendix E's explicit derivation showing that arbitrary bounded model weights can obtain certification with O(R) Gaussian noise. These are limited mathematical edits.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the first-order, black-box nonconvex certification and PL generalization claims. The introduction adds a recommendation that rewinding should replace finetuning or gradient ascent as a comparison baseline for deep-network unlearning.

C2.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B.3 newly attribute reconstruction instability beyond roughly half the training trajectory to accumulated approximation errors. v6 also adds practical noise/budget selection guidance and explains why D2D's reliance on an attracting global minimum does not extend to general nonconvex objectives. Appendix C's existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v6 replaces the anonymous code-repository address with the authors' repository, reports concrete storage requirements, and documents the LLM model, LoRA use, and epoch budgets. The original implementation details remain. Checklist removal drops the explicit MIT-license and eICU ethics-course disclosures.

R1.justification: v6 adds citations for Mistral, LoRA, and Alpaca, expands its positioning against D2D/finetuning, and explicitly claims the first treatment of nonconvex unlearning generalization in Appendix A.2.1. Most related work and the underlying novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact, with localized explanatory additions around rewinding, parameter choices, and results. Appendix B gains reconstruction and LLM subsections, moving the previous additional-results subsection to B.5. The NeurIPS checklist is removed and the conference footer updated.

P2.justification: v6 adds four appendix tables and Figure 5, clarifies captions, and groups Table 3 by certification status. It fixes the overlap between prose and Algorithms 1–2 on v4 page 5. Existing Figures 1–4 retain their plotted content. New Figure 5's caption reverses the panel identities relative to the plot titles.

improvement.justification: v6 supplies missing reconstruction accuracy/runtime evidence and an explicit instability caveat (B.3), making the black-box option easier to assess, and fixes v4's overlapping algorithm text. The gains are limited by the preliminary LLM evaluation, which lacks retained-task utility and uncertainty reporting, and Figure 5's caption error. The core guarantees and original benchmark results remain essentially unchanged.
